column1: log K = log10(1e9 / M) + log10(n) - log10(Kd in uM), M = 66,463 g/mol for albumin

Read the Route column. Rows reach their log K by different routes, from a direct measurement to a conversion resting on an assumed stoichiometry. Two values in this column are not necessarily the same kind of number.

ligand:protein ratio is the molar loading the measurement was made at. Below ~0.01 the assay sees the specific site; above ~1 it increasingly sees non-specific partitioning. It is NOT always PFAS conc / protein conc: for Allendorf 2019 the column is the paper's own reported v, bound per protein, and for ITC studies the two concentrations are in different vessels.

Wu 2024 is NOT in this sheet. Its ten HSA fluorescence-quenching rows are a named holdout in scripts/excluded_sources.py and were already absent from every figure; as of 2026-11-13 they are out of this sheet too. They were its only negative log K values and set its lower bound alone. The rows, and the full audit, remain in db/protein_binding.csv.

Beesoon 2015 is reduced to its LINEAR isomers. It is the only isomer-resolved source here; every other paper reports PFOA or PFOS on material of unstated isomer composition, so a branched row has no counterpart to be compared with. Linear supplies 98.5-99.99% of the bound pool even in technical ECF material, so it is also the right stand-in for a mixture. The branched rows stay in db/protein_binding.csv.
Gao 2025 is reduced to one row per compound, the no-added-salt condition; its full four-level salt series is in db/albumin_logK_with_conc.xlsx.
Moro 2022 is reduced to the representative row per compound: tightest site class, 37 C where usable.
